<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<title>Node.js Interview Mastery</title>
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Atkinson+Hyperlegible+Next:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,700;1,400&family=Bricolage+Grotesque:opsz,wght@12..96,500..800&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500;600&family=Caveat:wght@600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
  /* study-theme v4 "whiteboard": the one stylesheet every guide uses. Edit here, then run
     `npm run study:upgrade` to apply it to every guide (lib.upgrade swaps each guide's <style> for this file).
     Token names are also used inside the SVG diagrams (dg*.mjs), so rename none of them. */
  :root{
    /* light: a whiteboard. Navy ink, blue marker for actions, green for done, yellow highlighter. */
    --bg:#F5F7FA;
    --panel:#FFFFFF;
    --panel-2:#EEF2F7;
    --border:#D3DAE5;
    --text:#14213D;
    --muted:#4F5D78;
    --accent:#1B55C5;
    --accent-ink:#FFFFFF;
    --accent-soft:#E4EDFC;
    --gold:#7A5200;
    --gold-soft:#FFF1B8;
    --ok:#126B4B;
    --ok-soft:#DDF3E9;
    --code-bg:#EEF2F7;
    --danger:#B42318;
    --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(20,33,61,.06), 0 4px 14px rgba(20,33,61,.04);
    --mono: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
    --sans: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', 'Atkinson Hyperlegible', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
    --display: 'Bricolage Grotesque', var(--sans);
    --hand: 'Caveat', 'Segoe Print', 'Bradley Hand', 'Comic Sans MS', cursive;
    --measure: 76ch;
  }
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){
    :root:not([data-theme="light"]){
      /* dark: a chalkboard. Chalk white text, chalk blue / yellow / green accents. */
      --bg:#101A19;
      --panel:#17231F;
      --panel-2:#1E2D29;
      --border:#33493F;
      --text:#ECF1EE;
      --muted:#A9B8B1;
      --accent:#93BCFF;
      --accent-ink:#0A1730;
      --accent-soft:#1D3048;
      --gold:#F0CF6B;
      --gold-soft:#3A3216;
      --ok:#7FD6A8;
      --ok-soft:#173327;
      --code-bg:#0C1513;
      --danger:#F5A99C;
      --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4);
    }
  }
  :root[data-theme="dark"]{
    --bg:#101A19;
    --panel:#17231F;
    --panel-2:#1E2D29;
    --border:#33493F;
    --text:#ECF1EE;
    --muted:#A9B8B1;
    --accent:#93BCFF;
    --accent-ink:#0A1730;
    --accent-soft:#1D3048;
    --gold:#F0CF6B;
    --gold-soft:#3A3216;
    --ok:#7FD6A8;
    --ok-soft:#173327;
    --code-bg:#0C1513;
    --danger:#F5A99C;
    --shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.4);
  }

  *{box-sizing:border-box;}
  html,body{margin:0;padding:0;}
  html{color-scheme:light dark; scroll-padding-top:16px;}
  body{
    background:var(--bg);
    color:var(--text);
    font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:16px;
    line-height:1.6;
    -webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;
    text-rendering:optimizeLegibility;
  }
  a{color:var(--accent); text-underline-offset:2px;}
  :focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:2px; border-radius:4px;}
  ::selection{background:var(--gold-soft); color:var(--text);}

  .app{display:flex; min-height:100vh;}

  /* ---------- Sidebar ---------- */
  .sidebar{
    width:288px;
    flex:0 0 288px;
    border-right:1px solid var(--border);
    background:var(--panel);
    padding:18px 14px 24px;
    position:sticky;
    top:0;
    height:100vh;
    overflow-y:auto;
    scrollbar-width:thin;
  }
  .side-top{display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:8px; margin:0 0 14px;}
  .home-link{display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; font-size:14px; font-weight:500; color:var(--muted); text-decoration:none; padding:6px 8px; border-radius:8px;}
  .home-link:hover{color:var(--accent); background:var(--accent-soft);}
  .theme-btn{font:inherit; font-size:15px; line-height:1; width:34px; height:34px; color:var(--muted); background:transparent; border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:8px; cursor:pointer;}
  .theme-btn:hover{color:var(--accent); border-color:var(--accent);}
  .brand{
    font-size:13.5px;
    line-height:1.45;
    color:var(--muted);
    padding:0 8px 16px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
    margin-bottom:14px;
  }
  .brand b{display:block; font-family:var(--display); font-size:19px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:-0.01em; color:var(--text);}
  .brand br{display:none;}
  .nav-item{
    display:flex;
    align-items:center;
    justify-content:space-between;
    gap:10px;
    width:100%;
    text-align:left;
    padding:9px 10px;
    border-radius:9px;
    border:1px solid transparent;
    background:transparent;
    color:var(--text);
    font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:15px;
    line-height:1.35;
    cursor:pointer;
    margin-bottom:2px;
  }
  .nav-item:hover{background:var(--panel-2);}
  .nav-item.active{background:var(--accent-soft); color:var(--text); font-weight:700; box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--accent);}
  .nav-num{font-size:12.5px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:var(--muted); width:20px; flex:0 0 20px;}
  .nav-item.active .nav-num{color:var(--accent);}
  .nav-label{flex:1;}
  .nav-count{
    font-size:12px;
    font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;
    color:var(--muted);
    background:var(--panel-2);
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    padding:1px 7px;
    border-radius:999px;
  }
  .nav-item.complete .nav-count{color:var(--ok); border-color:var(--ok); background:var(--ok-soft);}
  .progress-box{
    margin-top:20px;
    padding:14px 12px;
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:12px;
    background:var(--panel-2);
  }
  .progress-box .label{font-size:12.5px; font-weight:700; color:var(--muted); margin-bottom:8px; text-transform:lowercase;}
  .progress-box .label::first-letter{text-transform:uppercase;}
  .progress-track{height:8px; border-radius:999px; background:var(--border); overflow:hidden;}
  .progress-fill{height:100%; background:var(--ok); width:0%; transition:width .25s ease;}
  .progress-num{margin-top:8px; font-size:13.5px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:var(--text);}
  .reset-btn{
    margin-top:10px;
    width:100%;
    font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:13px;
    color:var(--muted);
    background:transparent;
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:8px;
    padding:7px 8px;
    cursor:pointer;
  }
  .reset-btn:hover{color:var(--danger);border-color:var(--danger);}

  /* ---------- Main ---------- */
  .main{
    flex:1;
    min-width:0;
    padding:40px 48px 96px;
    max-width:1080px;
  }
  .hero{margin-bottom:36px;}
  .hero .eyebrow-free{display:none;}
  .hero h1{
    font-family:var(--display);
    font-size:clamp(28px, 3.4vw, 40px);
    line-height:1.12;
    margin:0 0 14px;
    font-weight:700;
    letter-spacing:-0.02em;
    text-wrap:balance;
  }
  .hero p{color:var(--muted); max-width:68ch; margin:0 0 6px; font-size:16.5px;}
  .hero p strong{color:var(--text);}
  .hero .source-note{font-size:13.5px; color:var(--muted); margin-top:18px; line-height:1.9;}

  .section-head{
    display:flex;
    align-items:baseline;
    gap:12px;
    margin:44px 0 14px;
    padding-bottom:12px;
    border-bottom:2px solid var(--text);
  }
  .section-head .num{font-family:var(--display); color:var(--accent); font-size:17px; font-weight:700; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}
  .section-head h2{font-family:var(--display); font-size:26px; line-height:1.2; margin:0; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:-0.015em;}
  .section-head .count{margin-left:auto; font-size:13.5px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; color:var(--muted); white-space:nowrap;}

  .qcard{
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:14px;
    background:var(--panel);
    margin-bottom:10px;
    overflow:hidden;
    box-shadow:var(--shadow);
  }
  .qcard:hover{border-color:var(--accent);}
  .qcard.open{border-color:var(--accent); box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent), var(--shadow);}
  .qcard.focused{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:1px;}
  .qhead{
    display:flex;
    align-items:flex-start;
    gap:14px;
    padding:15px 18px;
    cursor:pointer;
    user-select:none;
  }
  .qcheck{
    margin-top:3px;
    flex:0 0 auto;
    width:20px;height:20px;
    border-radius:6px;
    border:1.5px solid var(--muted);
    display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;
    cursor:pointer;
    background:var(--panel);
  }
  .qcheck:hover{border-color:var(--ok);}
  .qcheck.done{background:var(--ok); border-color:var(--ok);}
  .qcheck.done::after{content:"✓"; color:var(--panel); font-size:13px; font-weight:700;}
  .qmain{flex:1; min-width:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:5px;}
  .qtext{flex:1; font-size:16.5px; line-height:1.4; font-weight:700;}
  .qtext.done-text{color:var(--muted); font-weight:500;}
  .qchips{display:flex; gap:6px; flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .qsec,.qcore{font-size:12px; padding:1px 8px; border-radius:99px; border:1px solid var(--border); color:var(--muted); background:var(--panel-2);}
  .qcore{color:var(--gold); border-color:var(--gold); background:var(--gold-soft);}
  .qsum{font-size:14.5px; color:var(--muted); line-height:1.5; max-width:var(--measure);}
  .qcard.open .qsum{display:none;}
  .qchevron{
    flex:0 0 auto;
    color:var(--muted);
    font-size:20px;
    line-height:1;
    transform:rotate(0deg);
    transition:transform .15s ease;
    margin-top:2px;
  }
  .qcard.open .qchevron{transform:rotate(90deg); color:var(--accent);}
  .qbody{
    display:none;
    padding:2px 22px 22px 52px;
    border-top:1px solid var(--border);
    font-size:16px;
    line-height:1.65;
  }
  .qcard.open .qbody{display:block; padding-top:18px;}
  /* Prose keeps a readable line length; tables, code and diagrams may use the full card width. */
  .qbody > p, .qbody > ul, .qbody > ol, .qbody > blockquote, .qbody > .callout, .qbody > h3, .qbody > h4{max-width:var(--measure);}
  .qbody p{margin:0 0 14px;}
  .qbody ul, .qbody ol{margin:0 0 14px; padding-left:22px;}
  .qbody li{margin-bottom:7px;}
  .qbody li::marker{color:var(--accent);}
  .qbody strong{color:var(--text); font-weight:700;}
  .qbody h3, .qbody h4{font-family:var(--display); font-size:17px; margin:20px 0 8px; letter-spacing:-0.01em;}
  code{
    font-family:var(--mono);
    background:var(--code-bg);
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    padding:0 5px;
    border-radius:5px;
    font-size:0.875em;
    overflow-wrap:anywhere;
  }
  pre{
    font-family:var(--mono);
    background:var(--code-bg);
    color:var(--text);
    padding:14px 16px;
    border-radius:10px;
    overflow-x:auto;
    font-size:13.5px;
    line-height:1.65;
    margin:0 0 16px;
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    tab-size:2;
  }
  pre code{background:none; border:0; padding:0; font-size:inherit;}
  /* syntax colouring added by the engine (comments, strings, keywords, numbers) */
  .tk-c{color:var(--muted); font-style:italic;}
  .tk-s{color:var(--ok);}
  .tk-k{color:var(--accent); font-weight:500;}
  .tk-n{color:var(--gold);}
  /* A diagram is a whiteboard (a chalkboard in dark mode): engine.js redraws the tidy SVG by hand
     (see "sketch" there) and this sets the board, the marker strokes and the handwriting. */
  .diagram{
    background:var(--panel);
    border:1.5px solid var(--border);
    border-radius:14px;
    box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 4px var(--panel), inset 0 0 0 5px var(--panel-2);
    padding:16px;
    margin:0 0 16px;
    overflow-x:auto;
  }
  .diagram svg{display:block; margin:0 auto; max-width:100%; height:auto;}
  /* Handwriting is sized by x-height (font-size-adjust) so it reads as large as the type it replaces.
     These values are the largest at which every label in every guide still fits its box:
     `node scripts/study/audit-diagrams.mjs` proves it, so re-run that after changing them. */
  .diagram svg.sk text:not(.sk-code){font-family:var(--hand); font-size-adjust:.50; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:.012em;}
  .diagram svg.sk text[font-family="var(--mono)"]:not(.sk-code){font-size-adjust:.60;}
  .diagram svg.sk text.sk-caps:not(.sk-code){font-size-adjust:.44;}
  .diagram svg.sk text[font-weight="600"]:not(.sk-code), .diagram svg.sk text[font-weight="700"]:not(.sk-code){font-weight:700;}
  /* Code and SQL are never handwritten (engine.js sketchIsCode): .sk-code keeps the authored type. */
  .diagram svg.sk .sk-s{stroke-width:1.9px; stroke-linecap:round; stroke-linejoin:round;}
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference){
    .diagram svg.sk .sk-d{animation:sk-draw .5s ease-out backwards; animation-delay:var(--d, 0ms);}
    .diagram svg.sk .sk-t{animation:sk-ink .35s ease-out backwards; animation-delay:var(--d, 0ms);}
  }
  @keyframes sk-draw{ from{stroke-dasharray:1; stroke-dashoffset:1; fill-opacity:0;} to{stroke-dasharray:1; stroke-dashoffset:0;} }
  @keyframes sk-ink{ from{opacity:0;} }
  /* The tidy original stays one click away (the switch under each diagram), drawn exactly as authored. */
  .diagram.tidy{background:var(--panel-2); border-width:1px; border-radius:12px; box-shadow:none;}
  .dg-bar{display:flex; justify-content:flex-end; gap:4px; margin:10px 0 -4px; position:sticky; left:0;}
  .dg-bar button{
    font:500 11.5px/1 var(--sans); color:var(--muted); background:transparent; cursor:pointer;
    border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:999px; padding:5px 9px;
  }
  .dg-bar button:hover{color:var(--text); border-color:var(--border);}
  .dg-bar button[aria-pressed="true"]{color:var(--accent); background:var(--accent-soft); border-color:transparent;}
  .dg-bar button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:1px;}
  .dg-bar button[data-dg="zoom"]{margin-left:6px; border-color:var(--border);}
  /* On a phone a 900-unit drawing squeezed into 300px is unreadable, so it keeps a readable size
     and scrolls sideways inside its board instead. */
  @media (max-width:760px){ .diagram svg{min-width:680px;} }
  /* Enlarged view (engine.js enlargeDiagram) */
  .dg-zoom{
    width:min(1500px, calc(100vw - 24px)); max-width:none; max-height:calc(100vh - 24px); padding:0;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:16px; background:var(--bg); color:var(--text); overflow:hidden;
  }
  .dg-zoom[open]{display:flex; flex-direction:column;}
  .dg-zoom::backdrop{background:rgba(10,16,30,.6);}
  .dg-zoom-top{
    display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; padding:8px 10px 8px 16px;
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--border); font:500 12.5px/1.3 var(--sans); color:var(--muted);
  }
  .dg-zoom-close{
    font:600 13px/1 var(--sans); color:var(--text); background:var(--panel); cursor:pointer;
    border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:999px; padding:9px 14px;
  }
  .dg-zoom-close:hover{border-color:var(--accent); color:var(--accent);}
  .dg-zoom-close:focus-visible, .dg-zoom-body:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:-2px;}
  .dg-zoom-body{overflow:auto; padding:14px;}
  .dg-zoom .diagram{margin:0;}
  .dg-zoom .diagram svg{width:100%; min-width:860px; max-width:none;}
  .dg-zoom .dg-bar [data-dg="zoom"]{display:none;}
  .diagram.lightbg{background:#F8FAFC; border-color:#CBD5E1;}
  .diagram.lightbg .codelabel{color:#334155;}
  .tag{
    display:inline-block;
    font-size:12px;
    color:var(--gold);
    background:var(--gold-soft);
    border:1px solid var(--gold);
    border-radius:6px;
    padding:1px 7px;
    margin-bottom:10px;
  }
  .tscroll{overflow-x:auto; margin:0 0 16px;}
  .tscroll > table.cmp{margin:0;}
  table.cmp{
    width:100%;
    border-collapse:collapse;
    margin:0 0 16px;
    font-size:14.5px;
    line-height:1.5;
  }
  table.cmp th, table.cmp td{
    border:1px solid var(--border);
    padding:9px 12px;
    text-align:left;
    vertical-align:top;
  }
  table.cmp th{background:var(--panel-2); font-size:13.5px; font-weight:700;}
  table.cmp tr:nth-child(odd) td{background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--panel-2) 45%, transparent);}

  .tbadge{display:inline-block; font-size:12px; font-weight:700; color:var(--gold); background:var(--gold-soft); border:1px solid var(--gold); border-radius:99px; padding:2px 10px; margin-bottom:10px;}
  .deeper{margin-top:16px; padding-top:12px; border-top:1px dashed var(--border); font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.9;}
  .deeper + .deeper{margin-top:2px; padding-top:0; border-top:0;}
  a.go{color:var(--accent); text-decoration:none; border-bottom:1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 35%, transparent);}
  a.go:hover{border-bottom-color:var(--accent);}

  .search{width:100%; box-sizing:border-box; margin:0 0 14px; padding:10px 12px; font:inherit; font-size:14.5px; color:var(--text); background:var(--bg); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:10px;}
  .search::placeholder{color:var(--muted);}
  .search:focus{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:1px;}
  .qcheck:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset:2px;}
  mark{background:var(--gold-soft); color:var(--text); border-radius:3px; padding:0 2px;}
  .toolbar{display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; align-items:center; gap:10px 16px; margin:0 0 18px; font-size:14px; color:var(--muted);}
  .toolbar .tmeta{font-size:13.5px; margin-right:auto;}
  .toolbar .tgroup{display:flex; gap:10px; align-items:center; flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .toolbar button{font:inherit; font-size:13.5px; color:var(--text); background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:8px; padding:6px 12px; cursor:pointer;}
  .toolbar button:hover{border-color:var(--accent); color:var(--accent);}
  .toolbar label{display:flex; gap:6px; align-items:center; cursor:pointer; white-space:nowrap;}
  .toolbar input{accent-color:var(--accent); width:15px; height:15px;}
  .empty{color:var(--muted); font-size:15px; padding:18px; border:1px dashed var(--border); border-radius:12px;}
  .pager{display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; margin-top:28px;}
  .pager button{font:inherit; font-size:14.5px; font-weight:500; color:var(--accent); background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:10px; padding:12px 16px; cursor:pointer; max-width:48%; text-align:left;}
  .pager button:last-child{text-align:right;}
  .pager button:hover{border-color:var(--accent); background:var(--accent-soft);}
  .back-btn{position:fixed; right:22px; bottom:22px; z-index:10; font:inherit; font-size:14px; font-weight:700; color:var(--accent-ink); background:var(--accent); border:0; border-radius:99px; padding:11px 18px; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.22);}
  .keys{display:inline-block; margin-top:6px;}
  kbd{font-family:var(--mono); font-size:11.5px; padding:0 5px; border:1px solid var(--border); border-bottom-width:2px; border-radius:5px; background:var(--panel); color:var(--text);}
  .hero-actions{margin-top:18px; display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:10px;}
  .fc-start,.toolbar .flash-btn{font:inherit; font-weight:700; color:var(--accent-ink); background:var(--accent); border:1px solid var(--accent); border-radius:10px; cursor:pointer;}
  .fc-start{font-size:15px; padding:10px 18px;}
  .toolbar .flash-btn{color:var(--accent-ink);}
  .toolbar .flash-btn:hover{color:var(--accent-ink);}
  .fc-start:hover,.toolbar .flash-btn:hover{filter:brightness(1.1);}
  button.fc-start.alt{background:var(--panel); color:var(--accent); border:1px solid var(--accent);}
  button.fc-start.alt:hover{background:var(--accent-soft); filter:none;}
  a.fc-start.alt{display:inline-block; text-decoration:none; background:var(--panel); color:var(--accent); border:1px solid var(--accent);}

  /* ---------- Flashcards ---------- */
  body.fc-lock{overflow:hidden;}
  .fc{position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:50; background:rgba(8,14,26,.6); display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:24px;}
  .fc[hidden]{display:none;}
  .fc-dialog{width:min(920px,100%); max-height:100%; display:flex; flex-direction:column; background:var(--panel); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:18px; box-shadow:0 24px 70px rgba(0,0,0,.4); outline:none;}
  .fc-head{display:flex; justify-content:space-between; align-items:flex-start; gap:12px; padding:18px 22px 12px;}

      q:"When would you absolutely NOT use Node.js?",
      a:`<p class="lede">Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine. It uses a non-blocking, event-driven architecture designed for scalable network applications.</p><p>For heavy, long-running CPU-bound tasks (video encoding, ML inference, 3D rendering). Node is single-threaded — a heavy CPU task blocks the Event Loop, freezing the entire server for all concurrent requests.</p><pre>// CPU-bound task BLOCKS the event loop — all other requests hang
app.get('/heavy', (req, res) => {
  // ❌ This blocks for seconds — no other request can be served
  const result = fibonacci(45);
  res.json({ result });
});

// ✅ Offload to Worker Thread
import { Worker } from 'worker_threads';

app.get('/heavy', (req, res) => {
  const worker = new Worker('./fibonacci-worker.js', {
    workerData: { n: 45 }
  });
  worker.on('message', (result) => res.json({ result }));
  worker.on('error', (err) => res.status(500).json({ error: err.message }));
});</pre><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> Mention Worker Threads as a mitigation, but note Go/Rust/C++ are natively better for CPU-bound work. This shows you understand Node's design, not just its API.</p>`

      q:"How does libuv relate to Node.js?",
      a:`<p>V8 parses and executes JavaScript. libuv is the C library providing the Event Loop and asynchronous I/O (file system, networking). It manages the thread pool for operations the OS can't do async.</p><ul><li><strong>V8 Engine:</strong> Parses JS → bytecode → machine code. Handles memory (heap/stack), garbage collection.</li><li><strong>libuv:</strong> Cross-platform async I/O. Provides event loop, thread pool, timers, signals, child processes.</li><li><strong>Thread Pool (default 4):</strong> Used for: fs operations, DNS lookups (dns.lookup), crypto (pbkdf2, randomBytes), zlib compression.</li><li><strong>OS-level async (no thread pool):</strong> TCP/UDP sockets, pipes, TTY. These use epoll (Linux), kqueue (macOS), IOCP (Windows).</li></ul><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> libuv's thread pool defaults to 4 threads (UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE). This handles fs operations, DNS lookups, and crypto. You can increase it up to 1024.</p>`

      a:`<p>V8 uses a generational garbage collector. Young objects are collected frequently with Scavenge; old objects are collected less often with Mark-Sweep-Compact.</p><ul><li><strong>Young Generation (Scavenge):</strong> Small space (~1-8MB). New objects live here. Uses semi-space copying — divides into 'from' and 'to' spaces.     {
      q:"List the Event Loop phases in order.",
      a:`<p>The Event Loop has 6 phases. Between each phase, the Microtask Queue is drained.</p><ul><li><strong>1. Timers:</strong> Executes setTimeout/setInterval callbacks whose threshold has elapsed.</li><li><strong>2. Pending Callbacks:</strong> Executes deferred I/O callbacks (e.g., TCP errors).</li><li><strong>3. Idle/Prepare:</strong> Internal use only.</li><li><strong>4. Poll:</strong> Retrieves new I/O events, executes I/O callbacks. Blocks here if nothing else is scheduled.</li><li><strong>5. Check:</strong> Executes setImmediate() callbacks.</li><li><strong>6. Close Callbacks:</strong> e.g., socket.on('close').</li><li><strong>Between EVERY phase:</strong> Drain the Microtask Queue (process.nextTick first, then Promise callbacks).</li></ul><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> The key insight many miss: process.nextTick() has HIGHER priority than Promises in the microtask queue. It runs before any Promise.then() callback.</p>`
    },
    {
      q:"What is the output of this code? (Classic interview puzzle)",
      a:`<p>This tests understanding of the event loop phases and microtask queue ordering.</p><pre>console.log('1. script start');

setTimeout(() => console.log('2. setTimeout'), 0);

Promise.resolve()
  .then(() => console.log('3. promise 1'))
  .then(() => console.log('4. promise 2'));

process.nextTick(() => console.log('5. nextTick'));

setImmediate(() => console.log('6. setImmediate'));

console.log('7. script end');

// OUTPUT:
// 1. script start
// 7. script end
// 5. nextTick         ← microtask (highest priority)
// 3. promise 1        ← microtask (after nextTick)
// 4. promise 2        ← microtask (chained)
// 2. setTimeout       ← timers phase
// 6. setImmediate     ← check phase (order with setTimeout is non-deterministic at top level)</pre><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> Execution order: synchronous code → process.nextTick → Promises → timers/setImmediate. In an I/O callback, setImmediate always fires before setTimeout(fn, 0).</p>`

    {
      q:"What is 'Event Loop starvation' and how do you prevent it?",
      a:`<p>Starvation occurs when a recursive process.nextTick() or tight synchronous loop monopolizes the event loop, preventing I/O callbacks from executing.</p><pre>// ❌ STARVATION: this prevents ALL I/O from processing
function recursive() {
  process.nextTick(recursive); // fills microtask queue forever
}
recursive(); // server stops responding

// ✅ FIX: use setImmediate to yield to the event loop
function safeRecursive() {
  setImmediate(safeRecursive); // allows I/O between iterations
}

// ✅ FIX: break CPU work into chunks
async function processLargeArray(items: any[]) {
  const CHUNK_SIZE = 1000;
  for (let i = 0; i < items.length; i += CHUNK_SIZE) {
    const chunk = items.slice(i, i + CHUNK_SIZE);
    processChunk(chunk);
    // Yield to event loop after each chunk
    await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
  }
}</pre>`

      q:"What is the Cache Stampede problem and how do you solve it?",
      a:`<p>When a popular cache key expires, thousands of requests simultaneously hit the DB to rebuild it, potentially killing the database.</p><pre>// ❌ Naive caching — vulnerable to stampede
async function getProduct(id: string) {
  let product = await redis.get(\`product:\${id}\`);
  if (!product) {
    product = await db.findProduct(id); // 1000 requests hit DB simultaneously!
    await redis.set(\`product:\${id}\`, JSON.stringify(product), 'EX', 300);
  }
  return JSON.parse(product);
}

// ✅ Promise Caching (Mutex/Coalescing) — only ONE DB query
const inflightRequests = new Map<string, Promise<any>>();

async function getProductSafe(id: string) {
  const cacheKey = \`product:\${id}\`;
  let product = await redis.get(cacheKey);
  if (product) return JSON.parse(product);

  // Check if another request is already rebuilding this cache
  if (inflightRequests.has(cacheKey)) {
    return inflightRequests.get(cacheKey); // wait for the first request
  }

  // First request — lock and rebuild
  const promise = db.findProduct(id).then(async (result) => {
    await redis.set(cacheKey, JSON.stringify(result), 'EX', 300);
    inflightRequests.delete(cacheKey);
    return result;
  });

  inflightRequests.set(cacheKey, promise);
  return promise;
}</pre><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> Alternatives: probabilistic early expiration (refresh cache before it expires), or background refresh with a soft TTL.</p>`

    await client.query('BEGIN');

      a:`<p class="lede">A request flows through middleware in the order it was registered. Each function either ends the response or calls <code>next()</code> to pass control on; the first match for the route then handles it.</p><pre>app.use(express.json());                 // 1. parse body

      q:"Synchronous vs Asynchronous microservice communication?",
      a:`<p>The choice fundamentally affects reliability, coupling, and scaling behavior.</p><ul><li><strong>Synchronous (REST/gRPC):</strong> Service A calls Service B and waits. If B is down, A fails. Requires circuit breakers, retries, timeouts. Use for: queries needing immediate responses.</li><li><strong>Asynchronous (RabbitMQ/Kafka/SQS):</strong> Service A publishes event, responds to user immediately. Service B processes eventually. Use for: everything that doesn't need an immediate response (emails, notifications, analytics, order processing).</li><li><strong>Event Sourcing:</strong> Store events, not state. Rebuild state by replaying events. Provides complete audit trail. Complex but powerful for financial, compliance systems.</li><li><strong>CQRS:</strong> Separate read and write models. Write side emits events, read side builds optimized projections. Scales reads independently of writes.</li></ul>`

    {
      q:"What is the Circuit Breaker pattern?",
      a:`<p>Prevents cascading failures in distributed systems. When a downstream service is failing, stop calling it and fail fast.</p><pre>// Simple circuit breaker implementation
class CircuitBreaker {
  private failures = 0;
  private lastFailTime = 0;
  private state: 'CLOSED' | 'OPEN' | 'HALF_OPEN' = 'CLOSED';

  constructor(
    private threshold: number = 5,    // failures before opening
    private timeout: number = 30000,  // ms before trying again
  ) {}

  async call<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    if (this.state === 'OPEN') {
      if (Date.now() - this.lastFailTime > this.timeout) {
        this.state = 'HALF_OPEN'; // allow one test request
      } else {
        throw new Error('Circuit breaker is OPEN — service unavailable');
      }
    }

    try {
      const result = await fn();
      this.onSuccess();
      return result;
    } catch (err) {
      this.onFailure();
      throw err;
    }
  }

  private onSuccess() {
    this.failures = 0;
    this.state = 'CLOSED';
  }

  private onFailure() {
    this.failures++;
    this.lastFailTime = Date.now();
    if (this.failures >= this.threshold) {
      this.state = 'OPEN';
    }
  }
}

// Usage
const paymentCircuit = new CircuitBreaker(3, 10000);
const result = await paymentCircuit.call(() => paymentService.charge(amount));</pre><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> In production, use libraries like opossum (Node.js circuit breaker). Mention that Kubernetes readiness probes + service mesh (Istio) can also provide circuit breaking at the infrastructure level.</p>`

      q:"How do you make service-to-service calls resilient in Node.js?",
      a:`<ol><li><strong>Timeouts on everything:</strong> <code>AbortSignal.timeout(ms)</code> on <code>fetch</code>, and socket and query timeouts on clients. A missing timeout turns a slow dependency into an outage.</li><li><strong>Retries only for safe failures:</strong> network errors, 502/503/504, 429 with <code>Retry-After</code>; not for 400s. Use exponential backoff with <strong>jitter</strong>, a small cap, and only for idempotent requests (or with an idempotency key).</li><li><strong>Circuit breaker:</strong> after enough failures stop calling for a while (open), then probe (half-open). Libraries such as opossum implement it.</li><li><strong>Bulkheads and limits:</strong> cap concurrent calls per dependency so one slow service cannot use every socket or worker.</li><li><strong>Fallbacks:</strong> cached or default data, or a clear degraded response, instead of an error page.</li></ol><pre>async function callWithRetry(url, { retries = 3, base = 200 } = {}) {
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000) });
      if (res.status < 500 && res.status !== 429) return res;        // success or a client error: do not retry
      throw new Error('retryable ' + res.status);
    } catch (err) {
      if (attempt >= retries) throw err;
      const delay = Math.random() * base * 2 ** attempt;              // full jitter
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
}</pre><div class="callout"><strong>Retry storms:</strong> retries multiply load on a struggling service. Combine backoff and jitter with a retry budget and a circuit breaker.</div><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> Also propagate a deadline (<code>X-Request-Deadline</code> or gRPC deadlines) so downstream calls stop working when the caller has already given up.</p>`
    }

      a:`<p>CJS and ESM have fundamentally different module loading behavior.</p><ul><li><strong>CommonJS (require):</strong> Synchronous, dynamic (can require inside if-blocks), returns a copy of the exported value. Default in Node.js (without 'type': 'module').</li><li><strong>ES Modules (import):</strong> Asynchronous, static (imports hoisted, enables tree-shaking), returns a live binding (reference). Default in browsers.</li><li><strong>'type': 'module' in package.json:</strong> Makes .js files ESM. Use .cjs extension for CommonJS files in ESM projects.</li><li><strong>Interop:</strong> ESM can import CJS modules. CJS cannot use top-level await or static import (must use dynamic import()).</li></ul><pre>// CommonJS
const { readFile } = require('fs');
module.exports = { myFunction };
module.exports.default = myFunction; // CJS default export

// ES Modules
import { readFile } from 'fs';
export { myFunction };
export default myFunction;

// Dynamic import (works in both CJS and ESM)

      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"   // CJS consumers

Ranges: <code>^1.4.2</code> allows 1.x.x at or above 1.4.2, <code>~1.4.2</code> allows 1.4.x, an exact version allows nothing else.</li><li><strong>The lockfile</strong> (<code>package-lock.json</code>, <code>pnpm-lock.yaml</code>) pins the exact tree. Commit it. Use <code>npm ci</code> in CI: it installs exactly the lockfile and fails if it disagrees with <code>package.json</code>.</li><li><strong>dependencies vs devDependencies:</strong> runtime versus build and test tools; <code>npm ci --omit=dev</code> for production images.</li><li><strong>npm vs pnpm vs Yarn:</strong> pnpm uses a shared content-addressed store and strict node_modules layout (faster, disk-friendly, catches phantom dependencies); workspaces support monorepos in all three.</li><li><strong>Supply chain:</strong> run <code>npm audit</code> and automated update PRs (Dependabot, Renovate), review new transitive dependencies, avoid abandoned packages, and be wary of install scripts (<code>--ignore-scripts</code> where possible).</li><li><strong>Overrides:</strong> the <code>overrides</code> field (pnpm: <code>pnpm.overrides</code>) forces a patched version of a transitive dependency.</li><li>Publishing: prefer provenance-enabled releases and 2FA on the registry account.</li></ul><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> If asked "why did the build differ between machines?": a missing or ignored lockfile, or a range that resolved to a newer release.</p>`

      q:"How does EventEmitter work, and what are its classic gotchas?",
      a:`<p class="lede"><code>EventEmitter</code> (from <code>node:events</code>) is the publish/subscribe primitive under streams, HTTP servers and sockets: register listeners with <code>on</code>, fire them with <code>emit</code>.</p><pre>import { EventEmitter, once } from 'node:events';

const bus = new EventEmitter();
bus.on('order', (o) => console.log('billing', o.id));
bus.on('order', (o) => console.log('email', o.id));
bus.once('ready', () => console.log('first time only'));

bus.emit('order', { id: 7 });          // listeners run synchronously, in registration order

const [payload] = await once(bus, 'done', { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });  // promise form</pre><ul><li><strong>Emit is synchronous.</strong> A slow listener blocks the emitter; hand off with <code>setImmediate</code> or a queue if needed.</li><li><strong>An unhandled <code>'error'</code> event throws</strong> and can crash the process. Enable <code>captureRejections</code> or handle errors inside the listener.</li></ul><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> Good analogy for the interview: an EventEmitter is an in-process message bus. It is not durable and not distributed, so for cross-service events use a real queue.</p>`

      q:"What is AsyncLocalStorage, and when do you use it?",

The classic use is a request id or user id available in every log line without passing it through every function.</p><pre>import { AsyncLocalStorage } from 'node:async_hooks';
const als = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string }>();

app.use((req, res, next) => {
  als.run({ requestId: crypto.randomUUID() }, next);   // everything downstream sees this store

export function log(msg: string) {

}</pre><ul><li>Good for: request ids and tracing (OpenTelemetry uses this), per-request database transactions, tenant or locale context, audit logging.</li><li>Context is lost only if you break the async chain (some callback-based libraries, native modules); wrap those with <code>AsyncResource</code>.</li><li>It has a small overhead, so do not create a store per tiny operation.</li></ul><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> Contrast with the alternative: passing a <code>ctx</code> argument through every function is explicit and testable; <code>AsyncLocalStorage</code> is implicit but keeps deep call chains clean.</p>`

      q:"Why do Node services behind a load balancer return random 502s, and how do keep-alive timeouts fix it?",
      a:`<p class="lede">A load balancer reuses idle TCP connections to your service. If <strong>Node closes an idle connection first</strong>, the balancer can send a new request on a socket that is being closed, and the client gets a 502. Node's <code>server.keepAliveTimeout</code> defaults to <strong>5,000 ms</strong>; an AWS ALB keeps idle connections for 60 seconds by default.</p><pre>const server = app.listen(3000);

// Node must keep idle connections open LONGER than the load balancer does
server.keepAliveTimeout = 65_000;   // > ALB idle timeout (60 s)
server.headersTimeout = 66_000;     // keep it above keepAliveTimeout</pre><ul><li>The rule: <strong>backend idle timeout > proxy idle timeout</strong>, so the proxy always closes first.</li><li><code>headersTimeout</code> limits how long Node waits for request headers (it answers 408 when exceeded); <code>requestTimeout</code> (default 300,000 ms) limits the whole request.</li><li>The same idea applies to Nginx, Envoy and Kubernetes ingresses: check each hop's idle timeout.</li><li>Symptoms: rare 502s under light, bursty traffic that disappear under steady load (connections rarely sit idle then).</li></ul><p><strong>Interview tip:</strong> This is a favourite "real incident" story: intermittent 502s, fixed with one line, found by comparing timeouts at each hop.</p>`

      q:"How do you find out why a Node.js service is slow (event-loop delay, CPU profiles, heap snapshots)?",
      a:`<ol><li><strong>Is the event loop blocked?</strong> Measure event-loop delay; high p99 delay means synchronous work is starving requests.</li><li><strong>Where is the CPU going?</strong> Take a CPU profile: <code>node --cpu-prof app.js</code> writes a <code>.cpuprofile</code> on exit that you open in Chrome DevTools as a flame chart. const h = monitorEventLoopDelay({ resolution: 20 });
h.enable();
setInterval(() => {
  // values are in nanoseconds
  metrics.gauge('event_loop_delay_p99_ms', h.percentile(99) / 1e6);

      q:"How do you process large data with async generators, Readable.from and stream pipelines?",
      a:`<pre>import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises';

let total = 0;
for await (const line of rl) total += Number(line.split(',')[2] ?? 0);

// 2) transform with an async generator inside pipeline (backpressure and errors handled for you)
await pipeline(
  createReadStream('events.ndjson'),
  async function* (source) {
    source.setEncoding('utf8');
    let buffered = '';
    for await (const chunk of source) {
      buffered += chunk;
      const lines = buffered.split('\\n');
      buffered = lines.pop();                              // keep the partial last line
      for (const l of lines) if (l.includes('"type":"purchase"')) yield l + '\\n';

    if (buffered.includes('"type":"purchase"')) yield buffered + '\\n';
  },
  createGzip(),
  createWriteStream('purchases.ndjson.gz'),

      a:`<p class="lede">Recent Node versions run <code>.ts</code> files by <strong>stripping type annotations</strong> (replacing them with whitespace) rather than compiling them. // ---- answer polish: colour code blocks and let wide tables scroll sideways on their own.
// A <pre class="plain"> (prompts, sample output) is never coloured; other blocks only when they look like code.
const CODE_SIGNS = /\b(const|let|var|function|return|import|export|class|interface|type|await|async|SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|CREATE|def|func|public|private)\b|=>|===|!==|\(\)\s*\{|;\s*$|<\/?[A-Za-z][\w.-]*[\s>]|^\s*(\$|npm|npx|git|docker|kubectl|curl|node|aws)\s/m;
const TOKEN_RE = /(\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|(?<![:\w])\/\/[^\n]*|(?<=^|\s)#(?=\s|!)[^\n]*)|("(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"|'(?:\\.|[^'\\\n])*'|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`)|\b(const|let|var|function|return|if|else|for|while|do|switch|case|break|continue|import|from|export|default|class|extends|implements|new|async|await|try|catch|finally|throw|typeof|instanceof|in|of|type|interface|enum|readonly|public|private|protected|static|as|satisfies|keyof|infer|yield|void|null|undefined|true|false|this|super|SELECT|FROM|WHERE|JOIN|LEFT|INNER|ON|GROUP BY|ORDER BY|LIMIT|INSERT|INTO|VALUES|UPDATE|SET|DELETE|CREATE|TABLE|INDEX|BEGIN|COMMIT|AND|OR|NOT)\b|\b(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\b/gm;
const escCode = (s)=> s.replace(/&/g,'&').replace(/</g,'<').replace(/>/g,'>');
function colourCode(pre){
  if(pre.dataset.hl || pre.children.length || pre.classList.contains('plain')) return;
  pre.dataset.hl = '1';
  const src = pre.textContent;
  if(src.length > 6000 || !CODE_SIGNS.test(src)) return;
  let out = '', last = 0;
  src.replace(TOKEN_RE, (m, c, str, k, n, at)=>{
    out += escCode(src.slice(last, at)) + '<span class="tk-' + (c ? 'c' : str ? 's' : k ? 'k' : 'n') + '">' + escCode(m) + '</span>';
    last = at + m.length;
    return m;
  });
  pre.innerHTML = out + escCode(src.slice(last));
}
// ---- sketch:start
// Whiteboard diagrams. Every diagram in every guide is authored as tidy boxes and arrows (dg*.mjs);
// this redraws it by hand when the card is rendered: edges bow and corners drift a little, arrowheads
// become open chevrons, neutral outlines become marker ink, and text is set in the handwriting face
// (theme.css). The wobble is seeded from each shape's own coordinates, so a diagram looks the same
// on every visit. Strokes draw in when the card opens (theme.css, off under reduced motion).
// preview-diagrams.mjs inlines this block, so keep it self-contained.
function sketchRng(seed){
  let s = (seed >>> 0) || 1;
  return ()=>{ s ^= s << 13; s >>>= 0; s ^= s >>> 17; s ^= s << 5; s >>>= 0; return s / 4294967296 - 0.5; };
}
const skN = (v)=> Math.round(v * 10) / 10;
// One hand-drawn stroke from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2): the ends stay put, the middle bows by up to `amp`.
function sketchSeg(x1, y1, x2, y2, r, amp){
  const len = Math.hypot(x2 - x1, y2 - y1);
  if(len < 8) return ' L' + skN(x2) + ' ' + skN(y2);
  const bow = Math.min(amp, len * 0.03) * 2 * r(), t = 0.5 + r() * 0.3;
  const nx = -(y2 - y1) / len, ny = (x2 - x1) / len;
  return ' Q' + skN(x1 + (x2 - x1) * t + nx * bow) + ' ' + skN(y1 + (y2 - y1) * t + ny * bow) + ' ' + skN(x2) + ' ' + skN(y2);
}
function sketchPath(from, d){
  const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
  for(const a of from.attributes){ if(!/^(x|y|width|height|rx|ry|x1|y1|x2|y2|d)$/.test(a.name)) p.setAttribute(a.name, a.value); }
  p.setAttribute('d', d);
  if(!p.hasAttribute('fill')) p.setAttribute('fill', from.tagName === 'line' ? 'none' : 'black');
  from.replaceWith(p);
  return p;
}
// Code and SQL are read character by character, so they are not handwritten: a label that looks like
// a snippet keeps the type it was authored in. Plain words, names and short calls such as main() are
// still written by hand, as you would on a board.
const SK_SQL = /\b(SELECT|FROM|WHERE|JOIN|UPDATE|SET|INSERT|INTO|VALUES|DELETE|CREATE|ALTER|DROP|TABLE|INDEX|BEGIN|COMMIT|ROLLBACK|EXPLAIN|ANALYZE|GROUP BY|ORDER BY|LIMIT|OFFSET|HAVING|FOR UPDATE|ON CONFLICT|RETURNING)\b/g;
function sketchIsCode(s){
  if(s.length < 4) return false;
  // A sentence that merely mentions code is still a sentence: mostly plain words means handwriting.
  const words = s.trim().split(/\s+/), plain = words.filter(w=> /^[“"'(]?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z’'-]*[)”"',.:!?]*$/.test(w)).length;
  if(plain >= 5 && plain / words.length >= 0.7) return false;
  const t = s.replace(/\b[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.js\b/g, ' ');                                               // Next.js, Node.js are names, not files
  if(/=>|[{}\[\]$`]|;\s*$|::|[!=<>]=|\w_\w|\s=\s|--[a-z]|<\/?[A-Za-z][\w.-]*[\s/>]/.test(t)) return true;  // operators, snake_case, flags, tags
  if(/\w\.\w+\(|\w\([^)]*[,"'.=][^)]*\)/.test(t)) return true;                                           // obj.method( … ) or a call with arguments
  if(/^(GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE|HEAD)\s+\/|(^|\s)\/[\w-]+\/[\w\/:-]*|\b[\w-]+\.(m?[jt]sx?|json|md|html|css|sql|ya?ml|env)\b/.test(t)) return true;   // requests, paths, file names
  return (t.match(SK_SQL) || []).length >= 2;                                                           // a SQL statement, not one keyword in a sentence
}
function sketch(svg){
  if(svg.classList.contains('sk')) return;
  svg.classList.add('sk');
  const num = (el, a)=> parseFloat(el.getAttribute(a)) || 0;
  // arrowheads: a filled triangle becomes an open chevron in the same colour
  svg.querySelectorAll('marker path').forEach(m=>{
    const pts = (m.getAttribute('d') || '').match(/-?\d*\.?\d+/g), fill = m.getAttribute('fill');
    if(!pts || pts.length !== 6 || !fill || fill === 'none' || m.getAttribute('stroke')) return;
    m.setAttribute('d', 'M' + pts[0] + ' ' + pts[1] + ' L' + pts[2] + ' ' + pts[3] + ' L' + pts[4] + ' ' + pts[5]);
    m.setAttribute('stroke', fill); m.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
    m.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1.2'); m.setAttribute('stroke-linecap', 'round'); m.setAttribute('stroke-linejoin', 'round');
    const mk = m.closest('marker'); if(mk) mk.setAttribute('overflow', 'visible');
  });
  const inDefs = (el)=> !!el.closest('defs, marker');
  svg.querySelectorAll('rect').forEach(el=>{
    if(inDefs(el)) return;
    const x = num(el, 'x'), y = num(el, 'y'), w = num(el, 'width'), h = num(el, 'height'), rx = num(el, 'rx');
    if(w < 22 || h < 14 || rx >= Math.min(w, h) / 2 - 1) return;          // tiny marks and pills stay as they are
    const r = sketchRng(x * 73856093 ^ y * 19349663 ^ w * 83492791 ^ h * 2971), j = Math.min(1.5, Math.min(w, h) * 0.05);
    const c = [[x, y], [x + w, y], [x + w, y + h], [x, y + h]].map(pt=> [pt[0] + j * 2 * r(), pt[1] + j * 2 * r()]);
    let d = 'M' + skN(c[0][0]) + ' ' + skN(c[0][1]);
    for(let i = 0; i < 4; i++){ const a = c[i], b = c[(i + 1) % 4]; d += sketchSeg(a[0], a[1], b[0], b[1], r, 1.6); }
    sketchPath(el, d + ' Z');
  });
  svg.querySelectorAll('line').forEach(el=>{
    if(inDefs(el)) return;
    const x1 = num(el, 'x1'), y1 = num(el, 'y1'), x2 = num(el, 'x2'), y2 = num(el, 'y2');
    sketchPath(el, 'M' + x1 + ' ' + y1 + sketchSeg(x1, y1, x2, y2, sketchRng(x1 * 73856093 ^ y1 * 19349663 ^ x2 * 83492791 ^ y2 * 2971), 1.8));
  });
  svg.querySelectorAll('path').forEach(el=>{
    if(inDefs(el) || !/^\s*M\s*-?[\d.]+[\s,]+-?[\d.]+(\s*L\s*-?[\d.]+[\s,]+-?[\d.]+)+\s*$/.test(el.getAttribute('d') || '')) return;
    const n = el.getAttribute('d').match(/-?\d*\.?\d+/g).map(Number);   // straight polylines only: arrows and connectors
    const r = sketchRng(n[0] * 73856093 ^ n[1] * 19349663 ^ n[n.length - 2] * 83492791 ^ n[n.length - 1] * 2971);
    let d = 'M' + n[0] + ' ' + n[1];
    for(let i = 2; i < n.length; i += 2) d += sketchSeg(n[i - 2], n[i - 1], n[i], n[i + 1], r, 2.2);
    el.setAttribute('d', d);
  });
  // ink and draw order: neutral outlines use marker ink; everything gets a small stagger for the draw-in
  const els = [...svg.querySelectorAll('path, circle, ellipse, polygon, rect, text')].filter(el=> !inDefs(el));
  const step = Math.min(24, 760 / Math.max(1, els.length));
  els.forEach((el, i)=>{
    el.style.setProperty('--d', Math.round(i * step) + 'ms');
    if(el.tagName === 'text'){
      el.classList.add('sk-t');
      const s = el.textContent;
      if(sketchIsCode(s)){ el.classList.add('sk-code'); return; }   // code stays in the type it was authored in
      if(s.length > 10 && !/[a-z]/.test(s)) el.classList.add('sk-caps');   // capitals are wide in a handwriting face
      return;
    }
    const stroke = el.getAttribute('stroke');
    if(!stroke || stroke === 'none'){ el.classList.add('sk-t'); return; }
    if(stroke === 'var(--border)') el.setAttribute('stroke', 'var(--muted)');
    el.classList.add('sk-s');
    if(el.tagName === 'path' && !el.hasAttribute('stroke-dasharray')){ el.setAttribute('pathLength', '1'); el.classList.add('sk-d'); }
    else el.classList.add('sk-t');
  });
}
// Both versions are kept: the authored ("tidy") SVG is never thrown away, and a switch under every
// diagram flips all of them between the whiteboard drawing and the tidy original. The choice is
// remembered across guides.
const SK_PREF = 'study-diagram-style';
let skMem = null;   // used when storage is blocked, so the switch still works for this visit
function diagramMode(){ if(skMem) return skMem; try{ return localStorage.getItem(SK_PREF) === 'tidy' ? 'tidy' : 'sketch'; }catch(e){ return 'sketch'; } }
function drawDiagrams(root){
  const mode = diagramMode();
  root.querySelectorAll('.diagram').forEach(box=>{
    box.querySelectorAll('svg').forEach(svg=>{
      if(!svg.__tidy) svg.__tidy = svg.outerHTML;              // the authored drawing, kept verbatim
      if(mode === 'sketch') sketch(svg);
      else if(svg.classList.contains('sk')){
        const t = document.createElement('div'); t.innerHTML = svg.__tidy;
        const fresh = t.firstElementChild; fresh.__tidy = svg.__tidy; svg.replaceWith(fresh);
      }
    });
    box.classList.toggle('tidy', mode === 'tidy');
    let bar = box.querySelector('.dg-bar');
    if(!bar){
      bar = document.createElement('div'); bar.className = 'dg-bar';
      bar.setAttribute('role', 'group'); bar.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Diagram style');
      bar.innerHTML = '<button type="button" data-dg="sketch">✎ Whiteboard</button><button type="button" data-dg="tidy">▭ Tidy</button>' +
        '<button type="button" data-dg="zoom" aria-haspopup="dialog">⤢ Enlarge</button>';
      bar.addEventListener('click', (ev)=>{
        const b = ev.target.closest('button[data-dg]'); if(!b) return;
        if(b.dataset.dg === 'zoom'){ enlargeDiagram(box); return; }
        try{ localStorage.setItem(SK_PREF, b.dataset.dg); }catch(e){ skMem = b.dataset.dg; }
        drawDiagrams(document);
      });
      box.appendChild(bar);
    }
    bar.querySelectorAll('button:not([data-dg="zoom"])').forEach(b=> b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.dg === mode)));
  });
}
// A diagram is drawn 900 units wide but a card column is narrower, so its labels end up small.
// "Enlarge" shows it in a dialog as wide as the window (and scrollable on a phone), in whichever
// style is selected. The dialog element gives focus trapping and Esc for free.
function enlargeDiagram(box){
  let dlg = document.getElementById('dgZoom');
  if(!dlg){
    dlg = document.createElement('dialog'); dlg.id = 'dgZoom'; dlg.className = 'dg-zoom';
    dlg.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Enlarged diagram');
    dlg.innerHTML = '<div class="dg-zoom-top"><span>Scroll to move around. Esc closes.</span>' +
      '<button type="button" class="dg-zoom-close">✕ Close</button></div><div class="dg-zoom-body" tabindex="0"></div>';
    dlg.addEventListener('click', (ev)=>{ if(ev.target === dlg || ev.target.closest('.dg-zoom-close')) dlg.close(); });
    document.body.appendChild(dlg);
  }
  const body = dlg.querySelector('.dg-zoom-body');
  body.innerHTML = '';
  const copy = document.createElement('div');
  copy.className = 'diagram' + (box.classList.contains('lightbg') ? ' lightbg' : '');
  box.querySelectorAll('svg').forEach(svg=>{ const t = document.createElement('div'); t.innerHTML = svg.__tidy || svg.outerHTML; copy.appendChild(t.firstElementChild); });
  body.appendChild(copy);
  drawDiagrams(body);
  if(dlg.showModal){ if(!dlg.open) dlg.showModal(); } else dlg.setAttribute('open', '');
}

// Answer length. A card may carry an extras block (scripts/study/extras.mjs) with a 15-second and a
// 60-second spoken version. The switch shows one at a time; "Full answer" is the card as written. The
// choice is one setting for every card and every guide. A card without the block gets no switch.
const DEPTH_PREF = 'study-depth-pref-v1';
let depthMem = null;   // used when storage is blocked, so the switch still works for this visit
function depthSeconds(words){ return Math.round(words / 2.5); }   // 150 words a minute
function depthMode(){
  if(depthMem) return depthMem;
  try{ const v = localStorage.getItem(DEPTH_PREF); return v === '15' || v === '60' ? v : 'full'; }catch(e){ return 'full'; }
}
function depthWords(el){ return (el.textContent || '').trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).length; }
function applyDepth(doc){
  const mode = depthMode();
  doc.querySelectorAll('.depth-bar').forEach(bar=>{
    const body = bar.parentElement;
    body.classList.toggle('depth-short', mode !== 'full');
    body.dataset.depth = mode;
    bar.querySelectorAll('button').forEach(b=> b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.dataset.depth === mode)));
    const t = bar.querySelector('.depth-time');
    if(mode === 'full') t.textContent = 'about ' + Math.max(1, Math.round(Number(bar.dataset.words) / 150)) + ' min spoken';
    else { const s = body.querySelector('.xdepths [data-depth="' + mode + '"]'); t.textContent = 'about ' + depthSeconds(s ? depthWords(s) : 0) + ' s spoken'; }
  });
}
function mountDepths(root){
  root.querySelectorAll('.xdepths').forEach(x=>{
    if(x.dataset.mounted) return;
    const body = x.closest('.qbody') || x.parentElement;
    x.dataset.mounted = '1'; x.hidden = false;
    const ladder = body.querySelector('.xladder');
    const full = depthWords(body) - depthWords(x) - (ladder ? depthWords(ladder) : 0);
    const bar = document.createElement('div');
    bar.className = 'depth-bar'; bar.setAttribute('role', 'group'); bar.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Answer length');
    bar.dataset.words = String(Math.max(1, full));
    bar.innerHTML = '<button type="button" data-depth="15" aria-pressed="false">15 s</button><button type="button" data-depth="60" aria-pressed="false">60 s</button><button type="button" data-depth="full" aria-pressed="false">Full answer</button><span class="depth-time"></span>';
    bar.addEventListener('click', (ev)=>{
      const b = ev.target.closest('button[data-depth]'); if(!b) return;
      try{ localStorage.setItem(DEPTH_PREF, b.dataset.depth); depthMem = null; }catch(e){ depthMem = b.dataset.depth; }
      applyDepth(document);
    });
    body.insertBefore(bar, body.firstChild);
    body.insertBefore(x, bar.nextSibling);

// The interviewer pushes: follow-up questions that get harder, one at a time.

// ---- predict:start
// Predict the output. A card shows a snippet and an empty <div class="predict">. The reader types what the
// snippet will print, locks it in, and only then does it run, in a Web Worker built from a Blob (so an
// infinite loop cannot freeze the page, and can be stopped). The same formatter and harness run in Node
// (check-predict.mjs), so the output printed on each card comes from the code path the reader uses.
function predictFormat(value, nested){
  const t = typeof value;
  if(value === null) return 'null';
  if(t === 'string') return nested ? "'" + value + "'" : value;
  if(t === 'bigint') return String(value) + 'n';
  if(t === 'function') return value.name ? '[Function: ' + value.name + ']' : '[Function (anonymous)]';
  if(t !== 'object') return String(value);
  if(value instanceof Error || Object.prototype.toString.call(value) === '[object Error]') return value.name + ': ' + value.message;
  if(Array.isArray(value)) return value.length ? '[ ' + value.map(function(x){ return predictFormat(x, true); }).join(', ') + ' ]' : '[]';
  const keys = Object.keys(value);
  return keys.length ? '{ ' + keys.map(function(k){ return k + ': ' + predictFormat(value[k], true); }).join(', ') + ' }' : '{}';
}
// The program text a worker runs. `post` names the function that sends a message ({line} or {done}).
function predictSource(code, post){
  return "'use strict';\n" + predictFormat.toString() + "\n" +
    "const __send = (line) => " + post + "({ line });\n" +
    "const __console = { log: (...a) => __send(a.map((x) => predictFormat(x, false)).join(' ')) };\n" +
    "const __err = (e, prefix) => __send(prefix + ' ' + (e && e.name ? e.name + ': ' + e.message : String(e)));\n" +
    "if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.on) {\n" +
    "  process.on('uncaughtException', (e) => __err(e, 'Uncaught'));\n" +
    "  process.on('unhandledRejection', (e) => __err(e, 'Uncaught (in promise)'));\n" +
    "} else if (typeof addEventListener === 'function') {\n" +
    "  addEventListener('error', (ev) => { if (ev.preventDefault) ev.preventDefault(); __err(ev.error || ev.message, 'Uncaught'); });\n" +
    "  addEventListener('unhandledrejection', (ev) => { if (ev.preventDefault) ev.preventDefault(); __err(ev.reason, 'Uncaught (in promise)'); });\n" +
    "}\n" +
    "try { (function (console) {\n'use strict';\n" + code + "\n})(__console); } catch (e) { __err(e, 'Uncaught'); }\n" +
    "setTimeout(() => " + post + "({ done: true }), 700);\n";
}
// Compares what the reader said with what it printed, line by line, judging the answer and not the spacing.
function predictCompare(predicted, actual){
  const said = String(predicted).split('\n');
  while(said.length && !said[said.length - 1].trim()) said.pop();
  while(said.length && !said[0].trim()) said.shift();
  const norm = function(s){ return s.replace(/\s+/g, '').replace(/[“”‘’"]/g, "'"); };
  const same = function(a, b){
    const x = norm(a), y = norm(b);
    if(x === y) return true;
    // a bare string written with quotes ("a" for a) is forgiven; a string written as a number is not
    return x.length > 2 && x[0] === "'" && x[x.length - 1] === "'" && x.indexOf("'", 1) === x.length - 1 && y.indexOf("'") < 0 && x.slice(1, -1) === y;
  };
  const n = Math.max(said.length, actual.length);
  const rows = [];
  let right = 0;
  for(let i = 0; i < n; i++){
    const s = i < said.length ? said[i] : '', p = i < actual.length ? actual[i] : '';
    const ok = i < said.length && i < actual.length && same(s, p);
    if(ok) right++;
    rows.push({ said: s, printed: p, ok: ok });
  }
  return { rows: rows, right: right, total: actual.length };
}
// Runs a snippet in a worker made from a Blob. Resolves with the printed lines, or null when this browser will not
// run code here. A run that is still going after 2 seconds is stopped.
function predictRun(code){
  return new Promise(function(resolve){
    const lines = [];
    let w = null, done = false, timer = 0, url = '';
    const finish = function(extra){
      if(done) return;
      done = true; clearTimeout(timer);
      try{ w.terminate(); }catch(e){}
      try{ URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }catch(e){}
      if(extra) lines.push(extra);
      resolve(lines);
    };
    try{
      url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([predictSource(code, 'postMessage')], { type: 'text/javascript' }));

function startWeakDeck(){
  if(fc.open) return;   // the #weak deep link retries its message for a few seconds; ignore repeats once the deck is open, or every retry would reset the user's progress in it
  const list = weakOnThisGuide();
  if(list.length) startDeck(list, 'Weak cards');
}
if(fcWeakBtn) fcWeakBtn.addEventListener('click', startWeakDeck);
// A deck named by card keys ("sec:idx"), opened from a link such as /sql#deck=sq1:0,sq1:1. The link's
// message is posted repeatedly for a few seconds, so ignore it once a deck is open; unknown keys are dropped.
function startKeyDeck(keys, title){
  if(fc.open || !Array.isArray(keys)) return;
  const list = keys.map(k=>{ const p = String(k).split(':'); return entry(p[0], Number(p[1])); }).filter(Boolean);
  if(list.length) startDeck(list, title || 'Your deck');
}
refreshWeakButton();
window.addEventListener('storage', (e)=>{ if(e.key === WEAK_KEY){ weak = readJSON(WEAK_KEY, {}); refreshWeakButton(); } });

document.getElementById('resetBtn').addEventListener('click', ()=>{
  if(!confirm('Clear all reviewed checkmarks?')) return;
  reviewed = {}; writeJSON(STORAGE_KEY, reviewed);
  INDEX.forEach(e=>{ delete titleDone[e.tkey]; }); writeJSON(TITLES_KEY, titleDone);
  renderNav(); renderContent(); updateProgress();
});

document.getElementById('heroMeta').textContent = DATA.length + ' sections · ' + totalQuestions() + ' questions' + (CORE.size ? ' · ' + CORE.size + ' marked ★ core (linked from ' + window.__STUDY__.core + ')' : '');
document.getElementById('fcCore').textContent = CORE.size ? '▶ Flashcards: all ★ core questions' : '▶ Flashcards: all ' + INDEX.filter(e=>e.section.id!=='quickref').length + ' questions';
// ---- solo:start
// /study/<guide>.html?card=sec:idx shows just that one card, so a page elsewhere on the site (a mock
// round, a plan) can embed a card in an iframe. The frame is told how tall the card is.
function soloKey(search){ const m = /[?&]card=([^&#]+)/.exec(search || ''); return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : null; }
function soloRender(key){
  document.documentElement.classList.add('solo');
  content.innerHTML = '';
  const p = key.split(':');
  const e = entry(p[0], Number(p[1]));
  if(!e){ const m = document.createElement('p'); m.className = 'empty'; m.textContent = 'This card has moved.'; content.appendChild(m); }
  else content.appendChild(buildCard(e, { open: true }));
  const post = ()=>{ try{ parent.postMessage({ type:'solo-height', card:key, height: Math.ceil(content.getBoundingClientRect().height) }, '*'); }catch(_){} };
  if(window.ResizeObserver) new ResizeObserver(post).observe(content);
  post();
}
// ---- solo:end
initListen();
const SOLO = soloKey(location.search);
if(SOLO){ soloRender(SOLO); updateProgress(); }
else { renderNav(); renderContent(); updateProgress(); }
